result.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
result.summary: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. We study the alternative, \emph{model-driven} context management, in which the model itself decides when and what to compact through a context API. We gave models control over their own context in \nooa, NVIDIA's open source agent harness, and compared the two strategies on document research and machine learning engineering across context budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. Models that use the context API effectively reach higher accuracy, often with fewer input tokens, especially at tight budgets: \textbf{GPT 6.1 nearly triples its score at a 32K budget} on OfficeQA Pro v2 (21\%~$\rightarrow$~56\%), and \textbf{Kimi gains with up to 41\% fewer input tokens}. Models differ widely, however, in how often they use the API, how aggressively they compact, and when they start compacting, and prompt changes shift that timing. Finally, we show that \textbf{inference engines can make model-driven edits cheaper}: by reusing the KV cache of the unchanged suffix after an edit, \textbf{we cut prefill compute by up to 15\% per request with no measurable change in accuracy}. Together, these results point to a new co-design frontier: models trained to manage their own context, served by inference engines that support KV cache editing.

AI.brief_summary: 研究让模型通过 context API 自主决定何时压缩上下文、压缩哪些内容，并在 8K–512K token 预算下与 harness 自动压缩对比；同时利用未改动后缀的 KV cache 复用降低编辑后的 prefill 成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时更新、保留什么」的自主上下文管理可供核查 LVR 中的工作区更新、证据保留与 STOP 决策，KV cache 编辑线索也可能涉及 latent 状态复用与一致性，但该工作面向纯文本 agent，迁移性需进一步判断。
